Nvidia in Talks to Invest in Perplexity AI at $30 Billion Valuation
US AI startup Perplexity AI is closing in on a new multi-billion-dollar equity financing round, with Nvidia in talks to participate. The round would value the company at over $30 billion, up more than 50% from its previous round. Founded in 2022 by three founders born in the 1990s, Perplexity began as an AI conversational search service. Its AI agent product, Perplexity Computer, launched in February 2026, has driven annualized revenue from under $250 million to over $750 million in eight months. Nvidia initially considered purchasing technology licenses and poaching employees, but ultimately pivoted to an equity investment. The logic: Perplexity's agent products consume massive computing power, which drives chip sales. The company plans an IPO in 2028, but a 40x price-to-sales ratio and dependence on third-party models pose valuation concerns.
US AI startup Perplexity AI is advancing a new equity financing round, with chip giant Nvidia now in talks to participate. According to The Information, the round is expected to raise several billion dollars, valuing the company at over $30 billion (approximately 202 billion yuan) upon completion—a more than 50% increase from the $20 billion valuation following its previous round.
Founded in 2022, the company's founding team is centered on three founders born in the 1990s. If this round closes, the company—which has grown to this scale in just four years—will become one of the highest-valued independent players in the AI search space.
Notably, Nvidia's initial consideration was not an equity investment. In early negotiations, Nvidia had planned to spend billions of dollars to purchase licenses for some of Perplexity's technology and absorb some of its employees. But the talks ultimately pivoted toward a more conventional equity investment path.
From Search to Agents: The Core Driver of the Valuation Surge
Perplexity initially entered the market with an AI conversational search service—users ask a question, and the system directly returns a synthesized answer with source links, rather than a traditional search engine's list of web pages. This model was once seen as a "Google killer," forcing Google to accelerate its own AI search efforts.
But the real catalyst pushing the valuation from $20 billion toward $30 billion is a product called Perplexity Computer.
On February 25, 2026, Perplexity launched Perplexity Computer, a cloud-based AI agent product for professional users capable of autonomously executing a wide range of complex computer-based tasks. The product now competes directly with similar agent offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.
This product has fundamentally reshaped the company's growth trajectory. In March 2026, Perplexity's annualized recurring revenue surpassed $450 million; by August, annualized revenue climbed further to over $750 million. At the start of 2026, that figure was still under $250 million. In less than eight months, revenue nearly tripled.
User scale is equally impressive. Perplexity executives say monthly active users across its search and agent tools have surpassed 100 million, including tens of thousands of enterprise customers.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has revealed in interviews that he uses Perplexity daily. But a multi-billion-dollar investment decision clearly cannot be explained by the CEO's personal preference alone.
The deeper business logic: the more tasks Perplexity Computer executes and the longer it runs, the more computing power it consumes. Perplexity has thus transformed from a search company into a major compute consumer—and Nvidia stands to sell more chips as a result.
The two companies' collaboration is already underway. Perplexity has said it will use Nvidia's Vera CPUs to run agentic AI queries, and has signed a chip usage agreement with CoreWeave, a cloud service provider heavily backed by Nvidia. According to the report, representatives from both sides now meet multiple times per week to discuss hardware and software development.
This "sell servers with one hand, invest in application entry points with the other" playbook is not new for Nvidia. In 2024, Nvidia began talks to invest in OpenAI, and in September 2025 the two formally announced a strategic partnership with Nvidia committing up to $100 billion toward OpenAI data center buildouts. In March 2025, Nvidia joined Microsoft in a new funding round for Anthropic, with Nvidia committing up to $10 billion.
According to PitchBook, Nvidia participated in nearly 67 venture deals in 2025, up from 54 in 2024. Many of those portfolio companies turned around and used the money to buy Nvidia GPUs.
In March 2026, Nvidia led the formation of the Nemotron Alliance, bringing star teams including Perplexity, Mistral, Cursor, and Thinking Machines into the same camp to share compute and data.
▲ Nvidia's investment commitments to leading AI application companies in recent years and the compute procurement relationship. Figures are publicly disclosed investment ceilings; the Perplexity round is still under negotiation.
This business model—selling compute on one end while investing in application entry points on the other—is at the center of Wall Street controversy. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon and other Wall Street analysts warn that the "circular financing" pattern, in which chipmakers invest in downstream customers who then use that money to buy chips, is amplifying market concerns about the sustainability of AI capital expenditure. Nvidia's up to $100 billion investment commitment to OpenAI is viewed as one of the most emblematic examples of this model. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pushed back, arguing that such partnerships constitute a virtuous cycle rather than a means of artificially inflating chip demand.
If the Nvidia-Perplexity deal ultimately closes, it would become yet another case study of this model—the two sides have not publicly disclosed whether there are direct binding terms between the equity investment and chip purchases, but Perplexity has already signed a chip usage agreement with CoreWeave and plans to use Nvidia Vera processors to run AI queries. That business relationship predates the equity investment.
Perplexity's fundraising pace is a textbook capital myth.
In September 2022, before the product had even launched, the company secured a $3.1 million seed round. In March 2023, it completed a $25.6 million Series A at a $150 million valuation. Entering 2024, the company completed a Series B (at a $520 million valuation), a unicorn round (valuation exceeding $1 billion), and a round with SoftBank participation (at a $3 billion valuation).
In 2025, the company completed three rounds, with the valuation soaring to $20 billion. Soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo also announced an investment at that time and became a global brand ambassador. By early 2026, another round pushed the valuation to approximately $21.2 billion. If this new round closes at a $30 billion valuation, it would mean the valuation has multiplied 200-fold in less than four years.
2025 (three rounds combined)
For Series A investors who entered at a $150 million valuation, the return over three and a half years is 200x. Even the last batch of investors who entered at the $21.2 billion valuation in early 2026 would see paper gains of roughly 40% at a $30 billion valuation.
However, high valuations bring high expectations. With annualized revenue of $750 million, a $30 billion valuation implies a price-to-sales ratio of roughly 40x. By comparison, OpenAI and Anthropic have both seen significant upward revisions in valuation and revenue this year: OpenAI completed a new round in March this year at an $852 billion valuation; according to Bloomberg, its annualized revenue surpassed $40 billion by August, implying a P/S ratio of about 21x. Anthropic completed a new round in May, lifting its valuation to $965 billion; according to TechCrunch, its annualized revenue reached $65 billion by late July, implying a P/S ratio of about 14.8x.
Perplexity's revenue growth is indeed more explosive—tripling in eight months. But a 40x P/S ratio can only be sustained if revenue continues to grow exponentially.
The more critical structural issue is that Perplexity does not develop its own foundation models. Its Sonar model is fine-tuned from Meta's Llama, and its core capabilities are built on multi-model routing and retrieval-augmented generation. Its highest-quality answers depend on third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI. If these models raise prices or restrict access, Perplexity's cost structure will come under pressure. It is simultaneously a customer of and a competitor to these "suppliers."
Nvidia's entry fills exactly this gap. Through the Nemotron Alliance, Nvidia is building its own open-source model ecosystem, and Perplexity is one of the alliance's core nodes. If Perplexity can increasingly rely on Nvidia-affiliated models rather than competitors, the $30 billion valuation would have a more solid foundation. This investment is both a financial bet and an ecosystem lock-in.
Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas has previously stated publicly that the company plans to pursue an IPO in 2028. This means this $30 billion valuation round is likely the second-to-last or even the final round before going public.
